Everybody came together and said, what do we need to do? to protect our country, support our troops, see our nation through this difficult time. And I really do believe that that strength of character is still there today in the elected representatives of the American people.

turn_text: Well, I just believe in the free market. I believe in the wisdom of the free marketplace to sort out opportunities. And so the principle that we've applied here in Indiana not just in post-secondary education where choice has been the order of the day. And I understand what people in this association had to deal with in terms of some of the critics that have come your way. But in Indiana from literally back in the 1990s, we've been expanding educational choice from kindergarten through 12th grade, and it's just the principle that I have. Milton Friedman and his wife Rose were two brilliant economists. And their foundation is actually based here in Indiana because he saw Indiana as something of a mecca for educational choice. And then you might say, well, why would Milton Friedman be that focused on school choice? He simply said this. He said, the United States doesn't survive without an educated citizenry. And it's a free market economist. He said, the only thing powerful enough to renew education in America is the free market. Is that if you empower parents to choose where their kids go to school, you empower Americans with the broadest range of choices. The marketplace will work. And so it's the bias that I brought to the institutions represented here. It's the bias I brought to higher education in Indiana, just having the broadest range of choices and opportunities. And we've had great success in the state of Indiana with what's now essentially a universal school choice in the state. And I really do believe that as I said at the podium, or maybe I left it out because I didn't want to talk too long. I think our schools ought to work just as well for kids that want to get a job, as kids that want to get a degree. And I just honestly believe more school choice, more opportunities for families at every level will facilitate that. And then it'll contribute to the vitality of our country, our economy, and more importantly, the well-being of our people.
